name: Ripretinib (GIST, fourth-line)

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental DRAFT, owner/device test only; not clinically activated). Doses reflect standard-of-care fourth-line dosing from general references; original wording, no proprietary guideline text reproduced.

biomarkers.KIT: switch-control inhibitor with broad activity across primary and secondary KIT / PDGFRA resistance mutations acquired after earlier tyrosine kinase inhibitors
biomarkers.note: Ripretinib is a switch-control tyrosine kinase inhibitor for advanced GIST after progression on at least three prior agents (imatinib, sunitinib, and regorafenib). It broadly suppresses KIT and PDGFRA activation loop and ATP-pocket resistance mutations. General reference (Standard Guidelines / DeVita / Harrison); no proprietary guideline text reproduced.

supportiveCare: Continuous oral dosing once daily; continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity - no fixed cycle count (represented here as days 1 to 28 of a 28-day cycle).
Manage alopecia, palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia (hand-foot skin reaction), and hypertension; interrupt or reduce for higher-grade events.
Assess for cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma / new skin lesions and for decline in cardiac ejection fraction.
Avoid strong CYP3A4 inducers where possible; antiemetic / G-CSF prophylaxis not routinely required for oral ripretinib monotherapy.
monitoring: blood pressure (TKI-associated hypertension) at baseline and each cycle
skin examination for hand-foot skin reaction and new cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma
cardiac ejection fraction at baseline and as clinically indicated
clinical / radiographic response assessment (CT; Choi or RECIST criteria)

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 3-4 palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia, hypertension, or other significant toxicity
doseModificationRules.text: Interrupt and resume at a reduced daily dose per labeling once recovered; discontinue for recurrent intolerance. Obtain clinical review.

doseModificationRules.condition: symptomatic decline in cardiac ejection fraction
doseModificationRules.text: Hold and re-evaluate cardiac function; resume at a reduced dose or discontinue per clinical judgment. Obtain clinical review.

drugs.name: Ripretinib
drugs.notes: Ripretinib 150 mg PO once daily, given continuously (represented as days 1 to 28 of a 28-day cycle) until progression or intolerance. Standard fourth-line dose for advanced GIST after imatinib, sunitinib, and regorafenib. Reduce or interrupt for hand-foot skin reaction, hypertension, or a fall in cardiac ejection fraction per labeling. Standard-of-care dosing from general references (Standard Guidelines / DeVita / Harrison); original wording, no proprietary guideline text reproduced.

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) / DeVita / Harrison, general reference
provenance.locator: standard fourth-line dose for advanced GIST (150 mg PO once daily)
